title: Find an element of a 2023 message by its path

blocks.text: The fraud team investigates disputed e-commerce purchases from the network's 2023 link. They have the messages, and they want to ask for one value at a time with the paths of 17.5, such as `104.0x03.0xDF10` or `55.0x9F27`, instead of reading hex dumps by hand. The messages come from other systems, and some of the disputed ones are damaged. A wrong value is worse than no value: the team acts on what the tool prints.

`DatasetFinder.find` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/DatasetFinder.java` already parses the path and looks tags up. It returns the bytes as upper-case hex, `null` when the message doesn't have them, and refuses with an `IllegalArgumentException`. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:
The comment on each says what it is for. About fifteen lines in total.

cases.says: a path finds a dataset's content or a tag inside a TLV dataset, and an absent field, dataset or tag gives null
malformed paths are refused, and so is a tag path into a bitmap dataset
in DE 55 the part after the field is a tag, because chip data carries no dataset envelope
dataset 0x70 is the last TLV dataset, and 0x71 the first bitmap one
a dataset is found by walking the envelopes from the start, never by searching for its identifier byte
a dataset whose length runs past the end of the field is refused, never cut to what is left
00 and FF met while walking are refused, because they are not dataset identifiers

origin.section: 17.5. A Path Names One Element at One Level

concepts: DE 55 is composite but carries raw BER-TLV with no envelope, so a reader must know which fields have one.
A path names one element at one level: after DE 55 comes a tag, after another field a dataset, then a tag only inside a TLV dataset; absent is not an error.
A reader walks the envelopes from the start, steps over unknown datasets by their length, and refuses overruns and the bytes 00 and FF.
